title: I made a prototype for generating pokemon-style worlds with ai
author: mizerr

comments.author: DisasterNarrow4949
comments.body:
This may be one of the most awesome game things that I've seem in my life.

So it generates the tileset, the map, the creatures, the abilities, the trainers and the creatures the trainers have?

This is absolutely flabbergastingly amazing. Good job.

What are your plans looking forward with this prototype?

replies.author: mizerr
replies.body:
Thank you so much! Yes, it generates exactly what you said plus the game name / title screen. 

The next steps for me are to add ai generated music that matches the theme, improve map generation, add more gameplay functionality like actually collecting the creatures. Then, I want to get it in the hands of some people to try out and give feedback.

A big goal for me is to find people to collaborate with which is one reason I'm sharing. It's just me building this prototype.

comments.author: Normal_Umpire_1623
comments.body: Very good work. This has immense potential.

replies.author: mizerr
replies.body: There are few layers of ai to it such as interpreting the theme, then an ai creates prompts for the new graphics, then generates new graphics, text, types of creatures etc. Then all the new info and assets are made functional for the game by aligning them, putting them into a tile set, implementing it all in the right places.

replies.author: Vladi-N
replies.body: Wonderful! What LLMs do you use? The world seems to be generated very fast, so everything runs locally?

comments.author: Kulimar
comments.body:
Nice! This was something I was trying out with o1. It handled a character sprite sheet well, but it just had trouble properly parsing background tile sets and recognizing which tiles were water vs land, etc. :p

[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1\_Q49FGM8YdQZhHerQmlVhG6Ux\_i564zc/view?usp=drive\_link](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_Q49FGM8YdQZhHerQmlVhG6Ux_i564zc/view?usp=drive_link)

  
I was going to try it again when o3 dropped, but it seems you've found a way around it. Curious to know your approach.
